title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: JENNA'S DOG
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Jenna Ortiz, a tire shop mechanic from Pueblo, Colorado.
Jenna could fix anything with four wheels.
Then she brought home something with four legs.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: UNDER THE BED
segments.quote: Wishing to be friends is quick work, but friendship is a slow ripening fruit.
segments.author: Aristotle
lines: At the shelter, she asked for an easy dog. She came home with Moose.
Moose was big, shaggy and scared of everything. He lived under the bed for a week.
Gus, the old shelter volunteer, told her what the Greek thinker Aristotle said:
Wishing to be friends is quick work, but friendship is a slow ripening fruit.
So Jenna ate dinner on the bedroom floor. On day nine, a cold nose touched her hand.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE RECLINER
segments.quote: All things are difficult before they are easy.
segments.author: Thomas Fuller
lines: Then Moose felt at home. So he ate her recliner.
Jenna stood in a cloud of foam, holding the shelter's phone number.
Her dad's workbench had a note from the English writer Thomas Fuller:
All things are difficult before they are easy.
She put the phone down and signed them up for Saturday dog classes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE SIT
segments.quote: The best is the enemy of the good.
segments.author: Voltaire
lines: In class, the other dogs sat like little soldiers. Moose sat on the trainer.
Jenna practiced for two hours, until they were both grumpy.
The trainer, Dee, smiled and quoted the French writer Voltaire:
The best is the enemy of the good.
So Jenna stopped chasing perfect. Five minutes a day. One good sit. One big cheer.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: FOURTH OF JULY
segments.author: Euripides
lines: On the Fourth of July, the first firework went boom, and Moose went through the screen door.
Jenna searched for hours.
Then she remembered the Greek playwright Euripides:
Leave no stone unturned.
She checked every yard and alley. She found him at the shop, hiding in a stack of truck tires.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE STORM
segments.quote: Anyone can hold the helm when the sea is calm.
segments.author: Publilius Syrus
lines: In August, a hailstorm hit. Moose shook. Jenna's own heart was pounding too.
Gus had told her about Publilius Syrus, a Roman writer who was born a slave:
Anyone can hold the helm when the sea is calm.
So she sat on the floor, breathed slow and talked softly.
Moose watched her face. Then he put his head in her lap and fell asleep.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE GREETER
segments.quote: Although the world is full of suffering, it is full also of the overcoming of it.
segments.author: Helen Keller
lines: At the shelter, a new dog was hiding in a corner, just like Moose once did.
Gus read a line from Helen Keller:
Although the world is full of suffering, it is full also of the overcoming of it.
So now, every Saturday, Moose is the shelter greeter. Calm, slow and very shaggy.
Scared dogs follow him out of the corner.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Be patient. Keep going. Aim for good. Search hard. Stay calm. Pass it on.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Be patient. Keep going. Aim for good, not perfect. Search everywhere. Stay calm. Pass it on.
I once tried dog school myself. The dog graduated. I did not.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
